109: - train variance 为 0；
110: - train std 为 0；
111: - train 标准化后仍只有 1 个 unique 值，标准化值为 0（脚本中对零标准差使用数值保护，不产生变化）。
113: 因此它们不能在当前单一路径时间序列中提供可识别的日期间变化贡献。它们可以作为该路径的元数据或固定边界条件，但不能凭 E3 结果证明 slope、width 或 length 改善了跨日期预测。
131: `length_km`、`elevation_drop_m`、`mean_slope`、`median_slope`、`width_m` 是将 68 个 reach 汇总后的单一路径摘要。在 E3 数据集中，它们对每个日期相同；因此即使 LSTM/T-CNN 的代码接收了它们，也不能从当前案例识别其跨日期贡献。
137: 因此，E3 不应被描述为已经证明 slope / width / length 改善 DSK 预测。更准确的表述是：E3 评估了动态输入，并在代码层面对 LSTM/T-CNN 暴露了路径级静态摘要；这些摘要在单一路径时间维上是不可识别常数。
151: - `NEXT_DOWN` 拓扑检查：`{'PASS' if topology_ok else 'FAIL'}`；
156: 每个 HydroRIVERS reach 是一个 spatial unit。节点至少保留 reach ID、order、length、elevation drop、mean/median slope 和 width，并保留来源字段。
172: 每个 reach 的 routing 参数可由 length、slope、width 进行约束或参数化。应优先使用低容量、可解释的逐 reach 传输结构，避免把 68 个 reach 当成可自由拟合的独立深层参数。
176: 使用 68-reach 有向图、reach static features、BYBLK boundary flow 和 basin-level meteorological forcing，预测下游 DSK。当前只有一个上下游案例，reach-level latent states 没有直接观测，因此模型容量必须保持低；不建议直接使用 68 节点深 GNN，以免产生不可识别的 latent dynamics。

173: Daily discharge at a downstream station affected by hydraulic control reflects upstream routing, ungauged intermediate inflow, and operational regulation. Reconstructing such discharge from a single upstream gauge is therefore an information-identifiability problem rather than solely a model-capacity problem. Using the Bayinbuluke–Dashankou reach of the Kaidu River as a case study, we distinguished P1, P1B, and P2 virtual-gauging protocols and evaluated four evidence groups: graph-message and topology audits, explicit lagged-boundary models, a continuous single-storage state model under retrospective nested leave-one-year-out evaluation, and a preregistered interval-snowmelt increment test. The same-day directed GNN obtained an NSE of {f3(R('A_GNN')['NSE'])} in the 61-day 2005 internal historical diagnosis, below the no-graph model ({f3(R('A_NG')['NSE'])}), indicating that ordinary graph messages did not constitute stable hydrological routing. A flexible nonnegative K10 lag model achieved NSE={f3(R('C_K10_LEGACY')['NSE'])} in the revealed 2005 internal period but fell to NSE={f3(R('D4B_primary')['NSE'])} in the frozen 2011 primary window, exposing collinearity-driven spike selection and weak temporal transfer. The single-storage model M2 reduced RMSE in all six held-out years, supporting the presence of long hydrological memory, but failed the preregistered annual water-balance and parameter-stability gates. M2C, which added a 14-day interval-snowmelt proxy, increased macro-mean NSE to {f3(m2c_macro['nse'])}; nevertheless, it was rejected because the 1979 underestimation worsened from {f2(years[('M2','1979')]['pbias'])}% to {f2(m2c_years['1979']['pbias'])}% PBIAS. Under the present daily data and evaluation protocols, a single upstream discharge series is insufficient for stable cross-year reconstruction of daily discharge at the controlled downstream target. Intermediate inflow and local control-state observations are the priority information needed to reopen model development.

## outputs/vhs_bd1m/bd1m_model_dataset_report.md

16: - BYBLK Q 与 DSK Q 均来自 `data\processed\timeseries.csv` 的 `obs_q`。
20: - 目标 `Q_target_dsk` 没有用作输入变量；它只作为输出标签保留。
26: 为满足“动态变量来自目标日前”的约束，本表没有直接复制 D1 的当日包含窗口，而是对已有 ERA5-Land 日值先 `shift(1)`，再计算滚动窗口：
33: - `future_information_leakage`：全部为 `False`。
41: - `length_km`：沿冻结 reach 长度求和，单位 km；
42: - `elevation_drop_m`：reach 高程下降量求和，单位 m；
43: - `mean_slope`：按 reach 长度加权的 `mean_slope_m_per_m`，单位 m/m；
44: - `median_slope`：reach 级 median slope 的中位数，单位 m/m；
45: - `width_m`：真实 SWORD v2 `width` 的路径 reach 算术均值，单位 m。
59: | `Q_target_dsk` | 0 | 0.000000% |
62: | `mean_slope` | 0 | 0.000000% |
63: | `median_slope` | 0 | 0.000000% |
64: | `width_m` | 0 | 0.000000% |
68: ## train / validation / test 候选年份
72: - train 候选：1978–1981；
73: - validation 候选：1982；
74: - test 候选：1983。

## outputs/vhs_bd1m/channel_slope_report.md

7: ` slope_i = (elevation_i - elevation_i+1) / distance_i `
9: 其中 `distance_i` 为相邻采样点间距离，单位为米；输出坡度为无量纲 `m/m`。本计算不使用 BYBLK 与 DSK 的站点高程差，也不使用 `212.61 km` 作为分母。

## outputs/vhs_bd1m/experiments/e35_e3_interpretation_report.md

21: - train variance 为 0；
22: - train std 为 0；
23: - train 标准化后仍只有 1 个 unique 值，标准化值为 0（脚本中对零标准差使用数值保护，不产生变化）。
25: 因此它们不能在当前单一路径时间序列中提供可识别的日期间变化贡献。它们可以作为该路径的元数据或固定边界条件，但不能凭 E3 结果证明 slope、width 或 length 改善了跨日期预测。
43: `length_km`、`elevation_drop_m`、`mean_slope`、`median_slope`、`width_m` 是将 68 个 reach 汇总后的单一路径摘要。在 E3 数据集中，它们对每个日期相同；因此即使 LSTM/T-CNN 的代码接收了它们，也不能从当前案例识别其跨日期贡献。
49: 因此，E3 不应被描述为已经证明 slope / width / length 改善 DSK 预测。更准确的表述是：E3 评估了动态输入，并在代码层面对 LSTM/T-CNN 暴露了路径级静态摘要；这些摘要在单一路径时间维上是不可识别常数。
63: - `NEXT_DOWN` 拓扑检查：`PASS`；
68: 每个 HydroRIVERS reach 是一个 spatial unit。节点至少保留 reach ID、order、length、elevation drop、mean/median slope 和 width，并保留来源字段。
84: 每个 reach 的 routing 参数可由 length、slope、width 进行约束或参数化。应优先使用低容量、可解释的逐 reach 传输结构，避免把 68 个 reach 当成可自由拟合的独立深层参数。
88: 使用 68-reach 有向图、reach static features、BYBLK boundary flow 和 basin-level meteorological forcing，预测下游 DSK。当前只有一个上下游案例，reach-level latent states 没有直接观测，因此模型容量必须保持低；不建议直接使用 68 节点深 GNN，以免产生不可识别的 latent dynamics。

11: 本阶段只冻结方法、参数 schema 和代码骨架，不训练正式模型，不输出正式 NSE/KGE/RMSE，也不根据 test 结果选择结构或范围。
20: 68 个 HydroRIVERS reach 按冻结上游到下游 `reach_order=1..68` 串联。边为冻结 `NEXT_DOWN` 顺序 `reach_i -> reach_i+1`，共 67 条边。每个 reach 是一个 spatial unit；不使用独立神经 embedding。
33: - `S_i = max(abs(median_slope_m_per_m) * 1000, epsilon_slope_m_per_km)`；
34: - `W_i = width_m`；
35: - `epsilon_slope_m_per_km = 0.01 m/km`，冻结；
36: - slope 不直接将负值送入幂函数；使用绝对值后施加正下限；
51: dStorage_i/dt = Q_in_i - Q_out_i
52: Q_out_i = Storage_i / tau_i
57: 离散积分使用日内 sub-stepping 的显式 Euler。储量单位为 `discharge-days`，流量输出和边界 forcing 使用每日平均流量单位。质量审计按每个日步验证：
60: storage_start + boundary_volume - storage_end - terminal_outflow_volume = 0
71: - 不使用测试集选择 substep，也不依据 test 调整稳定规则。
88: Storage_i(0) = tau_i * Q_BYBLK(first_train_day)
91: 不使用未来 DSK Q，不使用 validation/test 初始化。正式训练时只能使用 train 起点和预注册参数；不得用未来观测反推初始状态。
99: - `R2`：68-reach physics-aware routing，`tau_i` 由 length/slope/width 的 4 参数共享公式确定。
101: 结构、参数范围和稳定规则不使用 test 选择。E4A 本阶段不训练 R0/R1/R2。
107: - train：1978–1981；
108: - validation：1982；
109: - test：1983。
111: test 不参与结构选择、参数范围选择、early stopping 或 hyperparameter selection。不得将 DSK target、未来 meteorological forcing 或未来状态用于边界和初始化。
115: `tests/test_bd1m_physics_routing.py` 覆盖：
118: - no future target leakage；
123: - identical reach test；
124: - constant inflow steady-state test。
128: E4B 仅在本协议冻结后进行，优先保持低容量。由于当前只有一个上下游案例，reach-level latent states 没有直接观测，不建议扩展为 68 节点深 GNN。可比较：

## outputs/vhs_bd1m/paper/e5c_results_clean.md

3: We first examined whether the reconstruction error could be reduced by introducing reach-scale heterogeneity into the routing model. The homogeneous 68-reach routing model (R1) achieved a training RMSE of 118.905, whereas the best numerically admissible heterogeneous-routing solution (R2) achieved an RMSE of 118.849. This corresponds to an improvement of only 0.047% relative to R1. The additional routing degrees of freedom therefore produced negligible improvement under the tested parameterization, despite substantially increasing model complexity.
6: The routing-only model showed a strong systematic tendency to underpredict DSK discharge during the 1982 development-validation period. R1 yielded an NSE of -1.434, an RMSE of 83.314, and a bias of -68.349, indicating that a large component of downstream discharge was not reproduced by upstream routing alone.
7: A simple mean-residual correction reduced the validation RMSE from 83.31 to 52.75, while a monthly residual climatology further reduced it to 49.06. The magnitude of this improvement, obtained without modifying the routing dynamics, indicates that a substantial and structured downstream contribution remained outside the routing-only representation. In particular, the improvement obtained from a purely seasonal baseline suggested that the missing component was not dominated by short-term routing errors alone.
9: To test whether the missing downstream contribution could be explained directly by incremental meteorological forcing, we compared precipitation-only, temperature-only, combined precipitation–temperature, and seasonal residual models on the 1982 development-validation period (Fig. 2).
11: These results show that the tested precipitation-history features did not explain the residual more effectively than a simple seasonal null. However, the apparently strong performance of raw temperature required additional examination because temperature itself is strongly seasonal. Therefore, the temperature result was treated as a diagnostic signal rather than evidence of an independent temperature-driven mechanism.
13: The temperature analysis was consistent with substantial shared seasonal information in this predictive setting. A six-harmonic Fourier seasonal correction achieved a validation RMSE of 45.468. After removing the expected seasonal component from temperature, the best season-plus-temperature-anomaly model produced an RMSE of 45.493, corresponding to a relative RMSE gain of -0.055%. Thus, adding temperature anomalies did not improve upon the seasonal Fourier baseline.
14: The raw temperature predictors were also highly redundant across temporal windows: the correlation between the 7-day and 30-day temperature features was 0.950 in training and 0.953 in validation. This redundancy is consistent with shared seasonal information, but does not by itself identify the source of the predictive signal.
15: Cross-year stability analysis provided an additional test. The raw T7 proxy outperformed Fourier6 in only one of the four leave-one-year-out experiments. Its RMSE gains relative to Fourier6 were -9.71%, -6.98%, -5.38%, and +4.45% for the 1978, 1979, 1980, and 1981 holdouts, respectively, yielding a median gain of -6.18%.
17: Taken together, these results indicate that raw temperature may function partly as a proxy for broader seasonal hydrological state in individual periods, but the evidence does not support a stable temperature-anomaly contribution beyond expected seasonality. We therefore selected the six-harmonic seasonal correction as the frozen correction model before evaluating the 1983 holdout.
19: After model selection was completed, the routing parameters, harmonic count, feature structure, and correction model were frozen before evaluation on 1983. No model refitting, harmonic re-selection, or test-based model selection was performed during this stage.
27: The external monthly series is numerically distinct from the 1978–1983 daily label series, but its primary provider, explicit unit metadata, and full provenance have not been independently resolved. Accordingly, these results are interpreted as an external monthly-series consistency evaluation, rather than as official independent hydrological validation.
29: Across the full diagnostic sequence, three consistent patterns emerged. First, increasing routing heterogeneity produced negligible additional fit, indicating that routing complexity alone was insufficient to resolve the reconstruction error. Second, a large fraction of the downstream residual exhibited strong and persistent seasonal structure. Third, although raw temperature provided strong predictive performance in individual periods, the tested temperature anomalies added no detectable benefit beyond the seasonal baseline, and the raw-temperature advantage did not remain stable across years.
39: The evidence supports the existence of this seasonal residual structure, but does not identify its unique physical origin. In particular, the present results do not distinguish among possible contributions from tributary inflow, snow or glacier melt, groundwater storage, reservoir operations, irrigation return flow, or other seasonally varying catchment processes.

## outputs/vhs_bd1m/paper/e5d_discussion_draft.md

3: The negligible improvement obtained by the heterogeneous routing model suggests that the dominant reconstruction error was not primarily caused by insufficient flexibility in reach-scale routing parameters. Although R2 introduced additional spatially varying exponents, its training RMSE improved by only 0.047% relative to the homogeneous R1 model. This indicates that, under the tested routing formulation, increasing parameter heterogeneity mainly added degrees of freedom without addressing the principal source of downstream discharge mismatch.
5: The conclusion should nevertheless be restricted to the present model structure and study reach. The result does not imply that routing heterogeneity is generally unimportant in river systems. Rather, it shows that, for the BYBLK–DSK reconstruction problem and the tested 68-reach routing parameterization, additional routing heterogeneity did not provide a practically meaningful solution.
7: A central result of the diagnostic sequence is that a substantial fraction of the downstream residual can be explained by a low-frequency seasonal component. Even a simple monthly residual climatology substantially reduced the routing error, and the smoother Fourier representation further improved the validation performance. The persistence of this signal across the development-validation stage, the 1983 frozen holdout, and the external monthly-series consistency evaluation indicates that the seasonal structure is not merely an isolated feature of one calibration period.
12: The strong performance of raw temperature features during the 1982 validation period initially suggested that temperature might provide useful explanatory information. However, the subsequent decomposition experiments changed this interpretation. Once the expected seasonal component was represented explicitly by the Fourier model, adding temperature anomalies produced essentially no additional improvement. The best seasonal-plus-temperature-anomaly model was slightly worse than the seasonal baseline.
14: A likely interpretation is that raw temperature acts as a proxy for broader seasonal hydrological state. Temperature covaries with snowmelt timing, evapotranspiration, vegetation activity, soil thermal conditions, and other seasonal processes. A statistical temperature predictor can therefore appear highly informative even when temperature itself is not the direct causal control on the missing discharge component.
17: The 1983 holdout provides the most important fixed-method test of the final correction. After the method was frozen, the seasonal correction reduced RMSE by 48.33% relative to routing alone, while improving NSE from -1.335 to 0.377. This demonstrates that the seasonal component retained substantial predictive value outside the development-validation period.   粘贴的文本 (1)
21: 4.5 External monthly consistency strengthens the evidence, but does not constitute official independent validation
23: However, this evidence has a clear provenance limitation. The primary provider, explicit unit metadata, and full documentary origin of the monthly workbook have not been independently verified. The monthly comparison should therefore be interpreted as an external consistency check rather than as official independent hydrological validation.
24: This limitation does not invalidate the comparison, but it changes the strength of the claim that can be made. The evaluation supports the robustness of the seasonal pattern across a numerically distinct data source, while stronger claims about independent validation require a traceable official observation source.
42: The remaining gap between the seasonal reconstruction and the observed daily hydrograph points toward the next methodological step: replacing the statistical seasonal surrogate with physically interpretable, time-varying incremental-flow components. A future model could combine routing with snow and glacier melt, local runoff generation, reservoir regulation, tributary inflow, and anthropogenic water use, while retaining the strict temporal validation protocol used here.

## outputs/vhs_bd1m/paper/e5e_methods_clean.md

4: The discharge dataset was divided chronologically into three fixed periods: 1978–1981 for model fitting and development, 1982 for development validation, and 1983 for fixed-method holdout evaluation. The test period was not used for parameter fitting, model selection, feature selection, or numerical-stability decisions.
5: The source audit confirmed complete day-to-day alignment between BYBLK and DSK throughout 1978–1983, and the downstream target was retained exclusively as a label rather than as an input feature.
7: The BYBLK–DSK pathway was represented by 68 sequential HydroRIVERS reaches connected by 67 directed edges. Reaches were ordered from upstream to downstream using the frozen NEXT_DOWN topology. Each reach was treated as one routing unit, and discharge leaving reach \(i\) became the inflow to reach \(i+1\).
8: No independently trained latent embedding was assigned to individual reaches. Instead, the routing experiment was deliberately kept low-dimensional to distinguish deficiencies in physical routing from missing catchment-scale inflow.
25: where \(S_i\) is reach storage and \(\tau_i\) is the reach residence time. The outlet discharge of one reach served directly as the inflow of the next reach.
46: where \(L_i\) is reach length, \(W_i\) is reach width, and
52: 1000\,|\mathrm{slope}_i|,
56: is the positive slope representation in m km\(^{-1}\). Parameter bounds were
65: 2.4 Numerical integration and state continuity
66: Routing was integrated using explicit Euler sub-stepping within each daily time step. The numerical stability constraint was
71: The routing state was initialized only once, at the beginning of the 1978 training period, using the steady-state condition
77: The internal reservoir states were then propagated continuously through 1978–1983. No state reinitialization was performed at the beginning of the 1982 validation period or the 1983 holdout period.
92: Routing parameters were fitted exclusively on the 1978–1981 training period using training RMSE as the optimization objective. Validation and test observations were not used in routing parameter estimation.
93: R1 optimized one shared residence-time parameter. R2 was optimized using multiple deterministic starting points under the predefined four-parameter bounds and numerical-admissibility constraints. The R2 analysis was treated primarily as a routing-complexity and identifiability diagnostic rather than as an opportunity for unrestricted parameter expansion.
94: The routing configuration, stability threshold, initialization rule, train–validation–test split, and objective function were defined before evaluating the fixed holdout. The final routing backbone was R1 with
100: The routing parameters were subsequently kept fixed during all residual-correction experiments, while reservoir states continued to evolve without reinitialization.
116: The 1982 development-validation experiments compared the following residual-correction classes:
140: The Fourier coefficients were estimated by ordinary least squares using only the 1978–1981 training residuals,
146: The six-harmonic Fourier configuration, rather than a temperature-based correction, was ultimately frozen before the 1983 evaluation. The frozen protocol specified six harmonics, ordinary least squares, fitting on 1978–1981 only, 1982 development validation, and no validation refit before the 1983 holdout.
147: To determine whether raw temperature provided information beyond seasonality, 7-day and 30-day temperature signals were decomposed relative to their expected seasonal component. Temperature-anomaly models were then evaluated jointly with the Fourier seasonal baseline. The temperature decomposition itself was fitted using training data only.
149: Because raw temperature performed strongly during the single 1982 development-validation year, its stability was further assessed within the training period using leave-one-year-out analysis across 1978–1981.
150: For each held-out training year, the seasonal and raw-temperature alternatives were fitted using the remaining training years and evaluated on the omitted year. This generated four within-training comparisons with overlapping fitting years and avoided using 1983 for model selection.
152: The final method-selection decision was based on the combined evidence from seasonal decomposition, within-training leave-one-year-out stability, and the development-validation analysis.
172: - development validation:
176: - no refitting on validation before test;
182: Previous provenance auditing showed that the monthly series is numerically distinct from monthly averages derived from the 1978–1983 daily DSK labels. However, the primary provider and explicit unit metadata of the workbook remain unresolved. Therefore, this analysis was treated as an external monthly-series consistency evaluation and not as official independent hydrological validation.
245: 2.13 Information-leakage and reproducibility safeguards
247: First, the temporal split remained strictly chronological: 1978–1981 for fitting, 1982 for development validation, and 1983 for fixed-method evaluation. This split and the prohibition on test-based model selection were defined before the final evaluation.
248: Second, DSK discharge was never used as an inference-time predictor. Meteorological historical windows used only pre-target information, and routing states were not initialized or corrected using validation- or test-period DSK observations.
249: Third, the routing state was propagated continuously across split boundaries rather than reinitialized at the beginning of validation or test periods.

## outputs/vhs_bd1m/paper/e5g0_intro_skeleton.md

7: - Topic: reliable streamflow information is required for water-resource decisions; ungauged and poorly gauged locations motivate information transfer and reconstruction.
15: - Sequence ML: B1-B3. Strengths: temporal dependencies, multi-basin learning and multiple timescales. Limits: prediction skill alone does not identify a local physical source.
16: - Graph/network ML: B4-B5. Strengths: topology-aware information exchange and routing. Limits: training targets and observation access affect interpretation and applicability.
18: - No claim that existing approaches are ineffective. Do not imply Transformer literature was reviewed; add a verified Transformer source if that family is retained in the eventual prose.
22: - SUPPORTED_COMPONENT: reconstruction errors can involve transport/routing representation, missing or biased local water inputs, and unresolved source/pathway contributions (C1, C3-C4, D1-D5).
24: - PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED_GAP: "Existing predictive workflows often emphasize improving model capacity, while the source of reconstruction error may remain mechanistically ambiguous."
25: - Evidence supports the possibility of ambiguity and the value of diagnosis, but not the word "often" as a field-wide prevalence statement. B2/B4/B6/C5 provide counterexamples to neglect of physics or interpretation. A systematic comparison of diagnostic practices is still needed for that broad sentence.
26: - Safe study-specific objective: distinguish, in the tested upstream-to-downstream configuration, insufficient routing representation from unresolved incremental downstream contribution, then test whether meteorological predictability adds information beyond a seasonal null.
32: - Describe the BYBLK-to-DSK reconstruction configuration and the tested homogeneous/heterogeneous routing formulations, without reporting performance.
34: - Fourier6 is a low-capacity seasonal residual representation; it is not a new hydrological mechanism or a physical source-identification model.
35: - Literature anchors: C1-C5 separate process/transport issues; D2 cautions against source attribution from aggregate flow; E1-E2/E5 motivate out-of-period evaluation; E6 motivates cautious proxy interpretation.
36: - Protocol: fit on 1978–1981; development validation in 1982; fixed-method holdout in 1983. No refitting on 1982 before holdout; no test-based model selection.
37: - Additional monthly comparison has unresolved primary provenance and explicit unit metadata; report external monthly-series consistency only.
41: - Contribution 1: a mechanism-oriented diagnostic framework distinguishing routing complexity from unresolved incremental downstream contribution under the tested parameterisation. This distinguishes error classes without assigning a definitive local physical source.
42: - Contribution 2: proxy-disambiguation using a seasonal null, temperature anomalies, training-year LOYO stability and moving-block-bootstrap uncertainty. These are predictive diagnostics, not causal identification.
43: - Contribution 3: strict freeze-before-holdout evaluation with 1978–1981 fitting, 1982 development validation and 1983 fixed-method holdout, plus a numerically distinct external monthly consistency check. No claim of universal generalisation or official independent hydrological validation.
49: - Event-scale and physical-source limitations belong in the study framing and Discussion; no detailed final performance numbers enter this skeleton.

## outputs/vhs_bd1m/paper/e5g1_introduction_clean.md

1: Continuous streamflow information supports understanding of river behaviour and water-resource decisions, yet prediction at ungauged or poorly gauged locations remains a demanding hydrological problem. Reconstructing a continuous hydrograph requires information about temporal variation, while flood and low-flow applications place additional demands on the representation of contrasting conditions. Reviews and comparative assessments of prediction in ungauged basins show that these tasks depend on available information, target-catchment characteristics and the conditions of hydrological transfer (He et al., 2011; Parajka et al., 2013; Salinas et al., 2013). Regionalisation addresses this problem by transferring observations, parameters or statistical relationships from gauged catchments to locations with insufficient direct information. Distance-based and regression-based approaches organise this transfer in different ways, with their usefulness depending on the application and catchment setting (He et al., 2011). Prediction skill also varies across climatic and landscape conditions, cautioning against assuming that success in one setting ensures comparable performance elsewhere (Parajka et al., 2013; Salinas et al., 2013). Learned regional relationships offer effective alternatives to conceptual-model regionalisation in the evaluated catchments (Arsenault et al., 2023). This literature motivates discharge reconstruction as a problem of transferring useful information within explicit spatial, temporal and methodological boundaries.
3: Approaches to this problem offer complementary representations of hydrological information. Conceptual and process-based models describe runoff production, storage and transport through prescribed relationships, while regionalisation extends their application beyond locally calibrated catchments (He et al., 2011). River-network models connect local runoff to downstream discharge through distinct delivery and transport stages, with alternative routing formulations and water-source tracking providing further detail (Mizukami et al., 2016; Grogan et al., 2022). Data-driven developments extend this spectrum through sequence models, topology-aware graph learning and hybrid physics–data architectures. LSTMs learn temporal dependencies and regional relationships, and entity-aware variants incorporate catchment attributes and examine learned basin similarities; multi-timescale architectures support predictions at different temporal resolutions (Kratzert et al., 2018, 2019; Gauch et al., 2021). Regionalisation comparisons demonstrate their predictive strengths within the tested catchments and model set (Arsenault et al., 2023). Graph-based approaches exploit connectivity through physics-guided surrogates and observation fusion or combine local runoff generation with graph routing, while hybrid spatially recursive models couple subbasin LSTM predictions to physics-based routing (Sun et al., 2022; Mosaffa et al., 2026; Yu et al., 2024). Distributed and differentiable frameworks also support spatial parameter estimation, adjoint calibration and modular process representation (Jay-Allemand et al., 2020; Colleoni et al., 2025). Previous work therefore already includes physics, topology, spatial modelling and interpretation. Routing studies further show that improved network representation can coexist with sensitivity to the supplied water budget (Nguyen-Quang et al., 2018), providing a basis for examining both predictive performance and information adequacy.
5: Within an upstream-to-downstream reconstruction problem, however, several sources of mismatch can remain difficult to distinguish. An upstream boundary describes water entering the represented pathway, whereas downstream discharge may also contain contributions generated within intervening catchments. Models that separate local runoff generation from channel transport make this distinction explicit, and water-source tracking illustrates how different origins can contribute to a simulated flow (Mizukami et al., 2016; Grogan et al., 2022). Routing representation is therefore one possible source of error, but an incomplete or biased water budget is another: revised ORCHIDEE routing captured seasonal variability while retaining biases associated with the supplied water budget (Nguyen-Quang et al., 2018). Potential contributions and modifications include groundwater discharge, tributary inflow, meltwater, storage changes and human water use, whose importance depends on the setting (Müller Schmied et al., 2021; Costelloe et al., 2015; Saberi et al., 2019; Van Tiel et al., 2021; Wiersma et al., 2022). These examples establish plausible sources of additional or altered flow, rather than identifying the processes responsible at a particular station. Source interpretation itself can be uncertain: groundwater mapping and tracer comparisons show that a hydrograph-based baseflow estimate need not uniquely resolve its physical origins (Costelloe et al., 2015). Predictive features also require care in interpretation. Differentiable-model comparisons show that useful inputs can act as proxies or identifiers rather than direct representations of physical processes; that finding concerns the tested features and does not establish the role of temperature in another application (Poudel and Steinschneider, 2026). Temporal-transferability studies further motivate evaluation beyond calibration conditions and separation of model selection from final assessment (Li et al., 2012; Nicolle et al., 2021; Patton et al., 2022). A diagnostic workflow is consequently useful for distinguishing transport inadequacy from unresolved downstream contribution and for testing whether apparently informative meteorological predictors contain information beyond simple seasonal structure.
7: This study investigates these questions along the tested BYBLK–DSK upstream-to-downstream configuration. We treat this setting as a virtual hydrological station reconstruction problem in which downstream discharge is inferred from upstream information and auxiliary hydrometeorological evidence. The objective is to examine whether the dominant mismatch is better explained by routing representation, unresolved downstream contribution or predictive proxies associated with seasonal structure. The diagnostic sequence moves from routing-complexity and downstream residual diagnosis through meteorological ablation and seasonality/proxy decomposition to cross-year stability and freeze-before-holdout evaluation. Homogeneous routing R1 is compared with heterogeneous routing R2 under the tested parameterisation, followed by residual and meteorological correction diagnostics. Fourier6, a six-harmonic seasonal null, serves as a low-capacity seasonal residual representation; temperature anomalies test incremental predictive information beyond that null. Training-year leave-one-year-out stability and moving-block-bootstrap uncertainty complement the development-period comparisons without assigning a physical source to the residual. The chronological design uses 1978–1981 for fitting, 1982 for development validation and 1983 for fixed-method holdout evaluation. Routing, correction structure and harmonic count are frozen before the holdout, with no refitting on 1982 before evaluating 1983 and no selection based on holdout performance.
9: The study makes three bounded contributions. One is a mechanism-oriented diagnostic framework distinguishing routing-complexity questions from unresolved incremental downstream contribution under the tested configuration, while retaining the possibility that transport, water inputs and other uncertainties interact. A second is a proxy-disambiguation sequence combining a seasonal null, temperature anomalies, leave-one-year-out stability and moving-block-bootstrap uncertainty. It tests incremental predictive information and cross-year consistency without treating a favourable development-period comparison as evidence of a separately identifiable physical mechanism. The third is a strict freeze-before-holdout protocol using 1978–1981 fitting, 1982 development validation and a 1983 fixed-method holdout, supplemented by a numerically distinct external monthly-series consistency check using frozen predictions. These contributions concern the assembled diagnostic sequence and its application to BYBLK–DSK. Their scope separates predictive usefulness from stronger claims about physical attribution or transferability to other periods and river systems.

## outputs/vhs_bd1m/paper/e5g1_introduction_draft.md

1: Continuous streamflow information provides a basis for understanding river behaviour and supporting water-resource decisions, yet obtaining useful predictions at ungauged or poorly gauged locations remains a demanding hydrological problem. The need extends beyond estimating a representative flow magnitude: reconstructing a continuous hydrograph requires information about temporal variation, while flood and low-flow applications place additional demands on the representation of contrasting flow conditions. Reviews and comparative assessments of prediction in ungauged basins show that these tasks depend on the available hydrological information, the characteristics of the target catchment and the conditions under which information is transferred (He et al., 2011; Parajka et al., 2013; Salinas et al., 2013). Regionalisation addresses this problem by transferring observations, model parameters or statistical relationships from gauged catchments to locations where direct information is insufficient. Distance-based and regression-based approaches provide different ways to organise that transfer, with their usefulness depending on the application and catchment setting (He et al., 2011). Comparative syntheses also show that prediction skill varies across climatic and landscape conditions, cautioning against assuming that an approach successful in one setting will retain the same performance elsewhere (Parajka et al., 2013; Salinas et al., 2013). More recent comparisons demonstrate that learned regional relationships can provide effective alternatives to conceptual-model regionalisation in the evaluated catchments (Arsenault et al., 2023). Together, this literature motivates discharge reconstruction as a problem of transferring useful information while retaining a clear account of its spatial, temporal and methodological limits.
3: Available approaches offer complementary representations of hydrological information rather than a simple division between physical and statistical prediction. Conceptual and process-based models describe runoff production, storage and transport through prescribed relationships, while regionalisation provides mechanisms for applying those relationships beyond locally calibrated catchments (He et al., 2011). River-network models additionally connect local runoff generation to downstream discharge: mizuRoute, for example, represents hillslope delivery and channel routing as separate stages, and the Water Balance Model provides alternative routing formulations alongside water-source tracking (Mizukami et al., 2016; Grogan et al., 2022). Sequence-learning methods offer another route to continuous prediction. Long short-term memory networks can learn temporal dependencies and benefit from regional training, while entity-aware architectures incorporate catchment attributes and analyse learned similarities among basins (Kratzert et al., 2018, 2019). Multi-timescale LSTM architectures extend this representation to predictions at different temporal resolutions (Gauch et al., 2021). Their demonstrated predictive strengths complement regionalisation comparisons in which LSTMs outperform the tested conceptual approaches, without establishing superiority across every hydrological setting (Arsenault et al., 2023). Graph-based models explicitly exploit network connectivity: physics-guided GNN surrogates combine simulated river states, observations and data fusion, whereas LSTM–GNN frameworks combine local runoff generation with graph routing (Sun et al., 2022; Mosaffa et al., 2026). Hybrid spatially recursive models likewise couple subbasin LSTM predictions to physics-based routing (Yu et al., 2024). Distributed and differentiable frameworks provide further opportunities for spatial parameter estimation, routing and process-based learning, including adjoint calibration and modular hydrological operators (Jay-Allemand et al., 2020; Colleoni et al., 2025). Thus, previous work already contains physics, topology, spatial modelling and interpretation. High-resolution routing studies also demonstrate the importance of network representation while retaining sensitivity to the water budget supplied to the routing scheme (Nguyen-Quang et al., 2018). These approaches supply substantive precedents for evaluating both predictive performance and the adequacy of the information represented.
5: Within an upstream-to-downstream reconstruction problem, however, several sources of mismatch can remain difficult to distinguish. An upstream boundary describes water entering the represented pathway, whereas downstream discharge may also contain contributions generated within intervening catchments. Models that separate local runoff generation from channel transport make this distinction explicit, and water-source tracking illustrates how different origins can contribute to a simulated flow (Mizukami et al., 2016; Grogan et al., 2022). Routing representation is therefore one possible source of error, but an incomplete or biased water budget is another: revised ORCHIDEE routing captured seasonal variability while retaining biases associated with the supplied water budget (Nguyen-Quang et al., 2018). Potential contributions and modifications include groundwater discharge, tributary inflow, meltwater, storage changes and human water use, whose importance depends on the setting (Müller Schmied et al., 2021; Costelloe et al., 2015; Saberi et al., 2019; Van Tiel et al., 2021; Wiersma et al., 2022). These examples establish plausible sources of additional or altered flow, rather than identifying the processes responsible at a particular station. Source interpretation itself can be uncertain: groundwater mapping and tracer comparisons show that a hydrograph-based baseflow estimate need not uniquely resolve its physical origins (Costelloe et al., 2015). Predictive features also require care in interpretation. Differentiable-model comparisons show that useful inputs can act as proxies or identifiers rather than direct representations of physical processes; that finding concerns the tested features and does not establish the role of temperature in another application (Poudel and Steinschneider, 2026). Temporal-transferability studies further motivate evaluation beyond calibration conditions and separation of model selection from final assessment (Li et al., 2012; Nicolle et al., 2021; Patton et al., 2022). A diagnostic workflow is consequently useful for distinguishing transport inadequacy from unresolved downstream contribution and for testing whether apparently informative meteorological predictors contain information beyond simple seasonal structure.
7: This study investigates these questions for discharge reconstruction along the tested BYBLK–DSK upstream-to-downstream configuration. The objective is to examine whether the dominant mismatch is better explained by the tested routing representation, an unresolved downstream contribution or predictive proxies associated with seasonal structure. The analysis follows a sequence of routing-complexity diagnosis, downstream residual diagnosis, meteorological ablation, seasonality versus temperature-proxy decomposition, cross-year stability assessment and evaluation after method freeze. Homogeneous routing, designated R1, uses a shared residence-time parameter across the represented reaches; heterogeneous routing, designated R2, tests additional reach-dependent variation under a specified parameterisation. Residual correction baselines then examine constant and seasonal structure before precipitation-only, temperature-only and combined predictor tests are considered. A six-harmonic Fourier seasonal null, termed Fourier6, serves as a low-capacity seasonal residual representation. Temperature-anomaly terms are evaluated relative to that null to distinguish incremental predictive information from the information already represented by seasonality. Leave-one-year-out analysis within the fitting years and moving-block-bootstrap uncertainty provide complementary checks on cross-year stability and uncertainty in the development-period comparison. These analyses concern predictive decomposition and do not assign a physical source to the residual. The chronological protocol uses 1978–1981 for fitting, 1982 for development validation and 1983 for fixed-method holdout evaluation. Routing, correction structure and harmonic count are frozen before the holdout, with no refitting on 1982 before evaluating 1983 and no selection based on holdout performance. This design makes the diagnostic decisions and the subsequent evaluation roles explicit.
9: The study makes three bounded contributions. One is a mechanism-oriented diagnostic framework that distinguishes routing-complexity questions from unresolved incremental downstream contribution under the tested configuration. Its purpose is to clarify which classes of explanation require further investigation, while retaining the possibility that routing, water inputs and other uncertainties interact. A second contribution is a proxy-disambiguation sequence combining a seasonal null, temperature anomalies, leave-one-year-out stability and moving-block-bootstrap uncertainty. This sequence asks whether meteorological predictors offer incremental information and whether their apparent advantage persists across fitting years, rather than treating a favourable development-period comparison as sufficient evidence of a separately identifiable mechanism. The third contribution is a strict freeze-before-holdout protocol using 1978–1981 fitting, 1982 development validation and a 1983 fixed-method holdout, supplemented by a numerically distinct external monthly-series consistency check. The monthly comparison uses the frozen predictions without estimating an additional bias adjustment from that series. Its unresolved primary provenance and explicit unit metadata restrict interpretation to consistency, while the daily holdout evaluates the fixed method in one additional year. The scope of these contributions is the assembled diagnostic sequence and its application to the BYBLK–DSK reconstruction problem. Their assessment separates evidence about predictive usefulness from stronger claims about physical attribution or transferability to other periods and river systems.

## outputs/vhs_bd1m/paper/e5h_abstract_draft.md

3: Reconstructing downstream streamflow from upstream observations can support virtual hydrological stations, but errors may reflect both routing limitations and unresolved contributions from the intervening catchment. Distinguishing these possibilities is essential before increasing model complexity or interpreting meteorological predictors. We present a diagnostic framework for upstream-to-downstream reconstruction in the BYBLK–DSK river system, comparing routing heterogeneity, residual baselines, meteorological forcing, and seasonal structure. Models were trained on 1978–1981 and examined using 1982 development validation, temperature-anomaly comparisons, leave-one-year-out analyses, and bootstrap uncertainty checks. A homogeneous routing backbone with a low-capacity six-harmonic Fourier residual correction was then frozen before evaluation on the 1983 daily holdout, without refitting or test-based selection. Under the tested parameterization, heterogeneous routing reduced training root mean square error (RMSE) by only 0.047%, whereas downstream residuals exhibited strong seasonal structure. Although raw temperature performed well in the development year, temperature-anomaly and cross-year analyses did not support stable incremental predictive benefit beyond seasonality; the raw-temperature model improved on the seasonal baseline in only one of four leave-one-year-out comparisons. The frozen correction reduced daily holdout RMSE by 48.33% relative to routing alone. An external monthly-series consistency evaluation yielded a 55.08% RMSE reduction using the same frozen predictions after aggregation, with unresolved source provenance and unit metadata limiting interpretation. The correction recovered much of the seasonal envelope, while summer event peaks remained imperfectly reconstructed. These findings support treating seasonality as a diagnostic baseline for unresolved downstream contribution rather than identifying a physical source process. The framework links model-complexity assessment, seasonal-proxy checks, and frozen temporal evaluation to a bounded interpretation of virtual hydrological station reconstruction.

## outputs/vhs_bd1m/paper/e5i0_conclusion.md

3: This study used a diagnostic sequence to examine upstream-to-downstream streamflow reconstruction in the BYBLK–DSK virtual hydrological station configuration. Under the tested parameterization, additional routing heterogeneity reduced training RMSE by only 0.047%. The routing-only underprediction and the improvement from simple residual corrections instead motivated examination of unresolved incremental downstream contribution. Seasonal baselines explained a substantial part of this mismatch, supporting a low-capacity representation of persistent seasonal residual structure.
5: Although raw temperature performed strongly in the development-validation year, temperature-anomaly comparisons, cross-year stability analysis, and supportive bootstrap uncertainty did not support stable incremental predictive benefit beyond expected seasonality under the tested specification. The selected homogeneous routing backbone and six-harmonic Fourier seasonal residual correction were therefore frozen before holdout evaluation, without refitting or test-based selection. On the 1983 daily holdout, the correction reduced RMSE by 48.33% relative to routing alone and recovered much of the broad seasonal envelope, while summer event peaks remained imperfectly reconstructed. The external monthly-series consistency evaluation added coarser-scale evidence, bounded by unresolved primary provenance and explicit unit metadata.
7: For this tested reconstruction, diagnosing the source of model error was more informative than simply increasing routing parameter complexity. The frozen seasonal correction provides a useful diagnostic surrogate for unresolved seasonal contribution, but not a physical source identification. Longer records, additional reaches, and independently documented process information are needed to assess broader transfer and improve event-scale reconstruction.

## outputs/vhs_bd1m/paper/e5i0_discussion_clean.md

5: The routing-complexity comparison provided little evidence that additional reach-routing heterogeneity could resolve the dominant mismatch under the tested parameterization. Training RMSE was 118.905450 for homogeneous R1 and 118.849295 for the best admissible R2 solution, a reduction of 0.047227%. R2 introduced reach-specific residence times through four globally shared parameters, rather than independently estimating a parameter for every reach. The result therefore concerns this constrained heterogeneity formulation and its training-fit gain. It does not establish that routing heterogeneity is generally unimportant or that alternative routing formulations and distributed parameterizations would perform similarly in other systems.
11: The progression from routing alone to mean-residual correction and monthly residual climatology indicates that the mismatch has both systematic magnitude and seasonal structure. Fourier6, the six-harmonic Fourier seasonal residual correction, provides a low-capacity representation of that structure. Its retained improvement on the frozen holdout is consistent with a seasonal pattern that extends beyond the development-validation year, within the observed record.
13: The seasonal residual correction should be interpreted as a statistical surrogate for unresolved seasonal contribution, not as a physical source model. Candidate explanations may include tributary or other lateral inflow, groundwater and baseflow variation, snow or glacier melt, storage changes, reservoir releases, and irrigation withdrawal or return flow. These are hypotheses for subsequent investigation; their presence or relative importance along BYBLK–DSK has not been established by the present experiments. A reproducible seasonal curve cannot distinguish among processes with overlapping seasonal timing. The correction is useful because it exposes a structured gap in upstream-only reconstruction, rather than because its harmonics identify the origin of downstream water.
17: Raw temperature performed strongly in the 1982 development validation, but that single-year comparison did not establish an independent temperature mechanism. The six-harmonic seasonal baseline achieved RMSE 45.468062, compared with 45.493273 for the best seasonal-plus-temperature-anomaly model. The experiments did not support a stable incremental predictive benefit of temperature anomalies beyond expected seasonality under the tested specification.
19: The training-year leave-one-year-out analysis further constrained interpretation of raw T7, the seven-day temperature predictor. It improved over Fourier6 in only 1/4 comparisons, with a median RMSE gain of -6.179175%. The supportive development-validation bootstrap also yielded a confidence interval crossing zero. These diagnostics address related predictive questions, but should not be treated as interchangeable tests of causality. In this predictive setting, raw temperature may function partly as a proxy for broader seasonal hydrological state. That possibility neither establishes temperature as merely a seasonal proxy nor excludes its physical influence on streamflow. More specific process information would be required to distinguish direct effects from shared seasonal variation.
23: The 1983 fixed-method holdout evaluated predictions after routing parameters, correction structure, coefficients, and harmonic count had been frozen. No development-validation refit or test-based model selection was performed. RMSE decreased from 87.161455 for R1 to 45.034412 for R1 plus frozen Fourier6, a reduction of 48.332194%. This supports substantial retained predictive improvement and temporal transfer outside the development-validation year for the tested reconstruction.
29: The external monthly-series consistency evaluation compares arithmetic monthly means of the same frozen predictions with the separately stored monthly DSK series. RMSE decreased from 77.754468 for R1 to 34.929611 for the frozen correction, a reduction of 55.077037%. This adds consistency-level evidence for the broad seasonal pattern at a coarser temporal scale. It does not provide an additional test of short-duration event reconstruction, and monthly aggregation can conceal discrepancies visible in the daily hydrograph.
31: The monthly series has a numerically distinct lineage from monthly means derived from the daily DSK labels. Numerical distinctness, however, does not establish observational independence or authoritative provenance. The primary provider and explicit unit metadata remain unresolved. The comparison is therefore an external monthly-series consistency evaluation, not official independent hydrological validation. No bias correction, parameter adjustment, or reinterpretation of the monthly values was applied. Stronger validation claims require traceable provider documentation, confirmed units, and an assessment of the relationship between the daily and monthly observation sources.
35: For the tested virtual hydrological station reconstruction, diagnosing model error was more informative than simply increasing routing parameter complexity. The predictive decomposition combines a routed upstream component with a seasonal residual correction representing unresolved incremental downstream contribution. This is a decomposition of the reconstruction, not an identified physical water-budget partition. Its usefulness lies in linking the routing-complexity test to residual structure, meteorological ablation, seasonal-proxy checks, and frozen evaluation.
37: The diagnostic sequence also helps bound model selection. Strong performance by a meteorological predictor in one development year is insufficient to infer a separately identifiable process or prefer it without stability evidence. Comparing predictors with a seasonal null, examining anomalies, and testing within-training cross-year consistency can reveal whether additional complexity provides sustained predictive information. The present case supports this workflow as a useful diagnostic strategy; it does not establish a generally superior reconstruction method across river systems.
41: The single BYBLK–DSK case limits spatial generalization, and six years of daily data provide limited coverage for long-term climate-regime testing. Fourier6 represents low-frequency seasonal structure rather than event-scale hydrological processes, and the study does not identify the unique physical origin of the residual. External monthly provenance and explicit unit metadata remain incomplete. In addition, R2 tests only one routing-heterogeneity parameterization, leaving alternative routing formulations and distributed parameterizations unevaluated.
43: Future work could examine explicit tributary and lateral inflow, snow or glacier process variables, groundwater and baseflow information, reservoir releases and storage, and irrigation withdrawal or return flow where independently documented. Longer records and replication on additional river reaches would permit broader temporal and spatial assessment. These directions are candidate investigations rather than claims that those processes are active in this reach. Any extension should preserve the frozen evaluation boundary and assess whether process-specific information improves the seasonal and event-scale reconstruction without relying on final-test performance for selection.

## outputs/diagnosis_2005_snapshot/stage_b/stage_b_diagnosis_report_zh.md

11: 1. **邻居消息是主要伤害来源；空图层代价很小。** 无图NSE=0.377；空边图层NSE=0.368（Δ=-0.009，小于种子标准差0.037）；近零消息门同样为0.368；固定0.05门降至0.364；真实边且关闭LayerNorm为0.323。完整数值见 `message_layer_ablation.csv`。
19: 2. **共享消息参数的监督来源错位，但“跨流域共享本身有害”尚未被性能消融证实。** 共享、删除塔里木边和独立流域层的NSE分别为0.311、0.311、0.310，几乎相同；塔里木预训练后冻结迁移为0.332，仍低于无图0.377。详见 `component_transfer_ablation.csv`。
32: 3. **塔里木—开都河共享消息参数是否有害？** 梯度审计确认塔里木主导消息层训练，但删除共享或改用独立层没有改善NSE；因此只能确认监督来源错位和负迁移风险，不能确认共享本身就是性能下降主因。
33: 4. **LayerNorm或图层结构是否有害？** 空边层相对无图仅下降0.009且小于种子波动；关闭LayerNorm比原含LayerNorm有向GNN约提高0.012，但仍比无图低0.054。它们有小幅影响，不是主要伤害来源。

## outputs/diagnosis_2005_snapshot/stage_d8/abstract_en.md

3: Daily discharge at a downstream station affected by hydraulic control reflects upstream routing, ungauged intermediate inflow, and operational regulation. Reconstructing such discharge from a single upstream gauge is therefore an information-identifiability problem rather than solely a model-capacity problem. Using the Bayinbuluke–Dashankou reach of the Kaidu River as a case study, we distinguished P1, P1B, and P2 virtual-gauging protocols and evaluated four evidence groups: graph-message and topology audits, explicit lagged-boundary models, a continuous single-storage state model under retrospective nested leave-one-year-out evaluation, and a preregistered interval-snowmelt increment test. The same-day directed GNN obtained an NSE of 0.311 in the 61-day 2005 internal historical diagnosis, below the no-graph model (0.367), indicating that ordinary graph messages did not constitute stable hydrological routing. A flexible nonnegative K10 lag model achieved NSE=0.853 in the revealed 2005 internal period but fell to NSE=0.138 in the frozen 2011 primary window, exposing collinearity-driven spike selection and weak temporal transfer. The single-storage model M2 reduced RMSE in all six held-out years, supporting the presence of long hydrological memory, but failed the preregistered annual water-balance and parameter-stability gates. M2C, which added a 14-day interval-snowmelt proxy, increased macro-mean NSE to 0.439; nevertheless, it was rejected because the 1979 underestimation worsened from -30.43% to -31.35% PBIAS. Under the present daily data and evaluation protocols, a single upstream discharge series is insufficient for stable cross-year reconstruction of daily discharge at the controlled downstream target. Intermediate inflow and local control-state observations are the priority information needed to reopen model development.
5: **Keywords:** virtual gauging station; controlled downstream station; graph neural network; lag collinearity; storage state; nested leave-one-year-out; cross-year evaluation
